mission.title: Install and Configure Docker Desktop Kubernetes
mission.description: Docker Desktop for Mac provides an integrated Docker experience on macOS, including a local Kubernetes cluster. It is ideal for developers looking to build and test applications in a Kubernetes environment without the overhead of managing a full cluster. However, it may not be suitable for production workloads due to resource constraints and performance limitations.

steps.title: Download Docker Desktop
steps.description:
This step installs Docker Desktop, which includes Kubernetes support.

```bash

open https://store.docker.com/editions/community/docker-ce-desktop-mac

```

> Download the latest version of Docker Desktop for Mac.

steps.title: Install Docker Desktop
steps.description:
Run the downloaded installer to set up Docker Desktop on your Mac.

```bash

open ~/Downloads/Docker.dmg

drag Docker to Applications

open /Applications/Docker.app

```

> Replace with the actual downloaded file name if different.
> This installs Docker Desktop.
> Launch Docker Desktop.

steps.title: Enable Kubernetes
steps.description:
This step configures Docker Desktop to enable Kubernetes support.

```bash

open -a Docker

sleep 10 && osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to tell process "Docker" to click menu item "Preferences…" of menu "Docker"'

osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to tell process "Docker" to click checkbox "Enable Kubernetes"'

osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to tell process "Docker" to click button "Apply & Restart"'

```

> Open Docker Desktop.
> Wait for Docker to start and open Preferences.
> Enable Kubernetes in the settings.
> Apply the changes and restart Docker.

steps.title: Verify Kubernetes Installation
steps.description:
Check if Kubernetes is running correctly on Docker Desktop.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> This command should show the Kubernetes node(s) in a Ready state.

uninstall.title: Uninstall Docker Desktop
uninstall.description:
This step removes Docker Desktop and all associated Kubernetes resources. Data loss may occur.

```bash

open /Applications

rm -rf Docker.app

rm -rf ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker

```

> Navigate to Applications.
> Remove Docker Desktop application.
> Remove Docker data and settings.

upgrade.title: Upgrade Docker Desktop
upgrade.description:
Backup your Docker settings, perform the upgrade, and verify the installation.

```bash

cp -r ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker.bak

open https://store.docker.com/editions/community/docker-ce-desktop-mac

open ~/Downloads/Docker.dmg

drag Docker to Applications

open /Applications/Docker.app

kubectl get nodes

```

> Backup Docker settings.
> Download the latest version of Docker Desktop.
> Open the downloaded installer.
> Replace the existing Docker application.
> Launch the upgraded Docker Desktop.
> Verify that Kubernetes is still running.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Kubernetes is not running'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Docker Desktop may not have started Kubernetes properly.

**Fix:**
Restart Docker Desktop and ensure Kubernetes is enabled in settings.

troubleshooting.title: kubectl get nodes returns 'No resources found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Kubernetes may not be initialized or running.

**Fix:**
Check Docker Desktop settings to ensure Kubernetes is enabled and running.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'context deadline exceeded'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Kubernetes may be taking too long to respond due to resource constraints.

**Fix:**
Increase the allocated resources for Docker Desktop in the settings.

troubleshooting.title: kubectl command fails with 'connection refused'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** Docker Desktop may not be running or Kubernetes is not initialized.

**Fix:**
Ensure Docker Desktop is running and Kubernetes is enabled.
